newsitem.title: UK: Tonnage short sparks firmer freight market.
newsitem.headline: Tonnage short sparks firmer freight market.

text.p: The BFI rose 12 points today to 1,465 amid reports of a widespread shortage of early vessels and firm rates paid for most categories of dry cargo tonnage.
Delays of upto 15 days were believed to apply for loading in Argentina, even before the main exporting season has begun.
Brokers mentioned renewed activity by Japanese charterers but some observers remain sceptical about optimistic assessments of marke prospects beyond the end of the year.
Relatively few new grain enquiries were seen and coal charterers were quiet. There were rumours of Hampton Roads coal to Rotterdam trading at $5.50 or less for January loading.

GRAIN - Timecharter is the order of the day, especially from US Gulf to the Far East. At least half a dozen Panamaxes were reported this morning having been booked on this route for delivery between mid Dec and mid Jan at rates between $13,500 to $14,750 daily plus between $275,000 and $320,000 bonus depending on type of vessel and position.

South Korean charterers were involved again in fixing and reletting Panamaxes for trips and period business. Joyous Age 69,271 dwt reported fixed last Friday to Hanjin delivery US Gulf end Dec for a trip Far East was understood relet to HMM, for example, and Success Bulker 64,000 dwt believed covered last week by Navios delivery Hong Kong for 3-5 months was rumoured relet to Hanjin.

The 1987-built Artemis 64,000 dwt was rumoured fixed delivery far east for 12 months on private terms. Grain charterer Shadab fixed Petriana 64,911 dwt delivery prompt Surabaya trip via S.Australia to Bin Qasim at $11,750 daily, reckoned by brokers to be a firm rate for a 1981-built vessel.

Fresh grain business today included Ocean Queen, Hong Kong with 54,000 heavy grain US Gulf/Taiwan for Jan 10/30 and Toepfer 50,000 wheat Bahia Blanca to Trincomalee for Dec 30/Jan 6. In the Handies there were reports of 30,000 heavy grain fixed US Gulf/S.Korea for Dec 15/25 at $30.00.

The Plate was very firm for these types with Romac, having fixed Nan Fung 34,000 dwt last week delivery W.Africa trip via E.C. South America redelivery skaw-passero at $6,500 daily, also taking the 1973-built Alexia 28,000 dwt delivery Recalada with the same redelivery at a strong $7,250 daily plus $125,000 bonus. Glencore quoted a new order for a prompt vessel for 22,000 heavy grain Plate/Cuba (which brokers said would be diffult to cover with the current acute shortage of vessels), and Andre quoted 13/15,000 wheat up River or Necochea to Mombasa for Dec 20/30. Elsewhere Toepfer quoted 15,000 wheat UK or North Continent/Israel for Dec 12/18, and Palmer Navigation 30,000 wheat Nopac/Yemen for Dec 27/Jan 17.

MINERALS - Caper rates in most areas continued firm but few fixtures were reported. In the Panamax size Kavo Kaliakra 64,861 dwt was rumoured fixed from Indonesia to Japan with coal, but details were not available.

Noble fixed Liman 52,580 dwt delivery W.Australia Dec 15/30 trip China at a modest $7,350 daily plus $80,000 bonus. A couple of manganese ore fixtures were said to have been concluded by Elkem to Norway - Alcinoe for 25,000/10 from Groote Eylandt in the low $20.00's and an unnamed vessel for the same quantity from Port Elizabeth at $11.00.

HANDY-SIZES - Moller fixed a Handymax and Pacific Carriers a 28/30,000 dwt craned bulker from the Continent to the Far East on privatterms. Van Ommeren were said to have relet Almar 39,197 dwt for unspecified Atlantic business, and E.D and F Man were linked with a 20-year old 33,000 dwt vessel delivery Skaw-Passero range for about 4 months Atlantic Trading at $6,000 daily. NYK were linked with a Topic 37,000 dwt craned bulker delivery east Australia trip Japan at about $7,500 daily plus unknown bonus. Halla were believed to have fixed Trade Master 24,000 dwt delivery Indonesia for 2-4 months at $5,400 daily, and Showa we said to have taken Handy Fabiana 24,000 dwt delivery Singapore trip Japan at $5,500 daily.
